title: Explorers and Settlers Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the brave explorers and faithful settlers who built America!

questions.question: Which Viking explorer reached North America around the year 1000 AD?
questions.explanation: Leif Erikson landed on the coast of North America around 1000 AD and called the land 'Vinland.'

questions.question: In what year did Christopher Columbus first sail to the New World?
questions.explanation: Columbus set sail in 1492 with three ships — the Niña, the Pinta, and the Santa María — and reached islands in the Caribbean Sea.

questions.question: What was the first permanent English settlement in America?
questions.explanation: Jamestown, Virginia, was founded in 1607 and was the first permanent English settlement in America.

questions.question: What agreement did the Pilgrims sign before going ashore at Plymouth?
questions.explanation: The Pilgrims signed the Mayflower Compact, an agreement to make fair laws and govern themselves based on Biblical principles.

questions.question: Who taught the Pilgrims how to plant corn and catch fish?
questions.explanation: God sent Squanto, a Native American, to help the Pilgrims survive by teaching them to plant corn and catch fish.

questions.question: Why did the colonists believe every child should learn to read?
options: So they could study the Bible
questions.explanation: The colonists believed reading was essential so that every person could study the Bible for themselves.

questions.question: What trail did Daniel Boone blaze through the Appalachian Mountains?
questions.explanation: Daniel Boone blazed the Wilderness Road through the Cumberland Gap, opening the way for settlers to move into Kentucky and beyond.

questions.question: What was the House of Burgesses?
options: The first elected government in America
questions.explanation: The House of Burgesses, created in 1619 in Virginia, was the first elected government in America and an important step toward self-government.
